newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish higher after GDP setback.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish higher after GDP setback.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished higher after recovering from an early setback tied to robust first-quarter growth.

June Treasury bond futures rallied sharply on Tuesday, but sank early today after the Commerce Department reported first-quarter growth up 5.6 percent, the highest gain since 6.0 percent in the fourth quarter of 1987.

June initially sank to 108-12/32, but quickly stabilized and crawled higher on a combination of sound short-term technicals and hopes for a U.S. budget deal. June rallied to a five-week high before slipping from the peak late.
Profit-taking late in the day pulled contracts from their highs, traders said, but overall, the day's recovery from early losses bolstered bulls.

"The sentiment is quite turned around," one Eurodollar trader said. "It's all changed completely in two days. They think that even if Fed officials do stick to their scenario of raising rates in May, that might be it for the year," he said.
Some traders said the market was now on sound technical footing, and pegged June T-bond resistance at 109-28/32 to 110-00.
Others urged caution ahead of more key data this week.

"I would say in a sense (the technical picture) is fairly sound, but the problem is I really don't want to judge it by one day," said Kurt Fraim, futures analyst with Aubrey G. Lanston. He said futures could lurch higher or lower, depending on how the data turn out.
"Today could be meaningless at eight o'clock on Friday," he said.

April non-farm payrolls will be released at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT on Friday, and were forecast up 211,000. April National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) data is scheduled for Thursday at 0900 CDT.
The NAPM index was forecast to slip to 53.6 in April from 55.0 in March.
Traders noted heavy volume in both Eurodollars and bond futures.

Traders said the futures arm of a French bank bought up to 10,000 June T-bonds, 15,000 10-year notes, and several thousand five-year notes. Traders said many good players were of both sides of the market.
In the GDP report, the first-quarter price index rose 2.7 percent and the implicit price deflator gained 2.3 percent, both above expectations.

At the close, June T-bonds were up 11/32 to 109-9/32, 10-year notes rose 12/32 to 106-31/32, September T-bills were up 0.015 at 94.460, September Eurodollars ended flat at 93.875 and December Eurodollars were 0.015 higher at 93.630. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
